Thanks Ben — I pulled the initial materials. High-level: there are a few compliance red flags that prevent us from giving a blanket green light without further vetting.

Summary of concerns:
- Jurisdiction: while UAE is not per se sanctioned, the customer indicates downstream partners in Koralia, which is on our restricted jurisdictions list. We need to confirm there will be no servicing or data transfer to Koralia.
- End-user details: we need formal KYC for the UAE subsidiary (entity registration, beneficial ownership, and proof of address).
- Intended use: clarify whether the model will be used for industrial automation or defense-related control systems — the latter requires export control review.

Ask from Compliance (by EOD Thu):
1) Ben — get UBO declaration + entity registration for AR Middle East FZ.
2) Ask Acme to confirm in writing they will not host or transfer service to Koralia or sanctioned end-users.
3) If use-case touches robotics control systems (safety-critical), escalate to Export Controls team.

Discount / terms: Approval of the 40% discount is a commercial decision that must be coordinated with Deal Desk and VP. From Compliance side, if the KYC + contractual mitigations are provided (geo-fencing, audit rights, indemnities), we can consider recommending a conditional exception for territory.

I’ll hold until we receive the documents. Copying Laura and Vivek for legal/exec visibility.

— Soojin

Appreciate the packet. Quick legal read: the documents are a good start but we should not sign the standard Master Services Agreement with the territory language as-is. Suggested path:

1) Conditional exception: allow UAE subsidiary to be a permitted entity for deployment provided the following are contractually locked before countersignature:
   - Explicit representation & warranty that no service will be resold or routed to Koralia or any sanctioned entity; breach = termination for cause.
   - Geo-fencing addendum (technical controls & monthly attestations).
   - Enhanced audit & logging rights for Redwood; right to suspend service on evidence of diversion.

2) Discount: recommend approving a 30% first-year discount (rather than 40%) tied to an annual commitment and payment milestone. Any deeper concession needs VP sign-off.

3) Operational requirements: require AML/KYC proof (UBO + registration), and a compliance onboarding call with their security officer.

If Compliance (Soojin) confirms no export-control red flags on the use-case and the UBO checks out, I will prepare the special terms language. Vivek — requesting sign-off on the proposed discount and territorial exception.

— Laura
